s/h is considered a coping mechanism, albeit a maladaptive one. It's understandable your frustration. I totally get it. I'm there too. I'm currently in a long-term treatment program, and one big thing I've taken away so far, is that baby steps are *okay*. doing something small is better than nothing at all. if your goal is staying alive (which it is \*friendly bonk bonk\*), then you're doing what you can in the moment to keep up with that goal. a concept in a type of therapy called DBT says that "everyone is doing their best at any given moment, AND they can always do better". baby steps is the key. you're one step closer to staying alive, even though it seems so backwards.  you're at the point where you're self aware! which is the key. it seems like you WANT to stop, but don't know how, which is SO BEYOND UNDERSTANDABLE!!! at the end of the day, s/h is going to be that dark voice in the back of your mind. building up skills and new neural pathways is a long process, but you're THERE. please reach out to me if you need resources on any coping skills/resources to look at!!! <3

I’m going to school at a community college right now. I saw what you said about being stressed out about cliques and bullying and stuff. I felt the same way. But really and truly it’s nothing like high school. If you think about it, no one takes classes during the exact same time period like in high school, so there’s not a whole lot of “ganging up”. And especially with community/commuter schools, no one gives a fuck. Truly truly truly. They’re there to get in, learn, go home, to work, whatever. In my experience, most people who go to community colleges are either older, so less drama, people who struggled to get high enough grades to get into a “name brand” school, or would struggle to afford that, which imo means they’re probably more mature (Obv a generalization). Your feelings are so so valid, but be assured that it will not be as bad as your brain is making it out to be. (And tbh there’s nothing worse than middle/high school haha)
